description: A flaw was found in Grafana.

In MIT krb5 release 1.14 and later (since authentication indicator support was added), an authenticated attacker can bypass authentication indicator requirements using an unkeyed checksum in the CAMMAC authdata container.
In MIT krb5 release 1.21 and later, server applications will erroneously treat the PAC within a ticket as verified when the server checksum is invalid.
In MIT krb5 release 1.15 and later, a client with kadmin administrative privileges can bypass the lockdown_keys attribute by using the password change protocol instead of the kadmin protocol.
In all released versions of MIT krb5, an unauthenticated attacker can cause a KDC process to perform a large read overrun, likely causing the process to terminate.

In MIT krb5 release 1.4 and later, an active network attacker can alter the arguments sent by a legitimate client to RPC services protected by RPCSEC_GSS, or cause return values to be sent in plain text.
If a KDC is configured to allow PKINIT authentication, an unauthenticated attacker can trigger a null pointer dereference, causing the process to terminate.
An SQL injection issue affects rsyslog deployments using the optional omclickhouse output module.
Recursive clones can lead to remote code execution through unsafe handling of submodule-related repository metadata.
